title: Optimal Strategies in Ranked-Choice Voting
source_inventory_policy: Curated inventory for the current partial-formalization review surface. It is not a claim that every source-visible result in the full paper is fully formalized; remaining source-model/proof boundaries are documented in the validation report and conditional-boundary sidecars.

paper_structure_classifier_constraints.statement:
-
Paper Appendix B.2 canonical generated constraints from a deterministic
order-and-sequence structure classifier.

paper_structure_partition.statement: - Paper partition condition from Proposition 2.1: with suitable tie-breaking, each voter-data point corresponds to exactly one structure.

paper_fstv_constraint_agreement.statement: - Paper equivalence from Proposition 2.1: the election result can be obtained either by running `F_STV` or by verifying satisfiability of the unique structure's constraints.

paper_final_order_realized_by_constraint.statement: - Paper final-order realization predicate: an order is obtained from voter data by satisfying the constraints of some structure.

paper_smart_allocation_slack_filling_fea.statement:
-
Algorithm 3 slack-feasibility formula: every required slack component is filled.

paper_smart_allocation_slack_filling_cos.statement:
-
Algorithm 3 slack-cost formula: total added votes across slack components.

paper_smart_allocation_slack_filling_alg.statement: - Algorithm 3 exact-fill allocation: fill every required slack exactly.

paper_reduce_ballot_by_removed_candidate.statement:
-
Algorithm 4 ballot reduction: delete every removed candidate from the ballot
while preserving the order of all remaining candidates.

paper_strict_support_count.statement:
-
Definition C.2 strict support: the number of voters whose ballots start in
`sources` and rank `candidate` before any candidate in `blockers`, represented
as the first-active count for active set `{candidate} ∪ blockers`.

paper_candidate_group_removal_condition.statement:
-
Algorithm 6 group-removal condition: every candidate in `group` remains below
quota after the budget is added to its strict support, and every candidate
outside `group` has strictly larger strict support after transfers from
`group \ {inside}`, also below quota.

paper_candidate_group_removal_safety.statement:
-
Algorithm 6 safety conclusion: the candidates in `group` remain below quota
after any budget-bounded addition, and every possible last eliminated member of
`group` remains below each outside candidate after the paper's strict-support
transfer accounting.

paper_irrelevant_candidate_concrete_redu.statement:
-
Paper Algorithm 4 concrete reduced-election specification: return exactly the
candidate-deletion instance and preserve active-support counts at the terminal
active set.

paper_reduce_election_instance_by_candid.statement:
-
Paper Algorithm 4 concrete reduction operation: remove candidates from the
candidate set and from every ballot.

paper_irrelevant_candidate_concrete_redu.source_location: paper-facing review target; exact source location to be refined

paper_sequence_reduction_concrete_covera.statement:
-
Paper Proposition 3.4 concrete coverage specification: the returned sequence
family covers every feasible source sequence.

paper_sequence_reduction_bounds.statement: - Algorithm 7 sequence bounds: upper wins and lower initial losses.
paper_sequence_reduction_bounds.source_location: paper-facing review target; exact source location to be refined

paper_sequence_reduction_bounds_from_pre.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 bounds formula: `UW` is the minimum of the seat count and the
predicted win-support capacity divided by quota; `iL` is the lower bound on
consecutive initial losses computed by Predict-Losses.

paper_predict_wins_candidates.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 Predict-Wins filter: candidates whose strict support from all
candidates, plus the budget, can exceed quota.

paper_predict_wins_support.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 Predict-Wins support accumulator: candidates are traversed in the
source order, each selected candidate contributes strict support with earlier
selected candidates treated as blockers, and the resulting support feeds the
upper-win formula.

paper_predict_wins_budget_accumulator_qu.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 prefix-form budgeted Predict-Wins condition: each predicted winner
reaches quota at the blocker state generated by the earlier predicted winners,
after adding the budget units assigned to that candidate.

paper_predict_wins_budget_ready_candidat.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 Predict-Wins ready set at a processed prefix: these are the
candidates that pass the current strict-support-plus-budget quota test after
the earlier predicted winners have been treated as blockers.

paper_predict_wins_ready_selections_of_s.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 Predict-Wins ready-set constructor from the source traversal
inequalities: each selected candidate is a source candidate and reaches quota
after its assigned budget at the blocker state determined by the already
processed winners.
paper_predict_wins_ready_selections_of_s.source_location: paper-facing theorem endpoint; proof details are discharged by the underlying Lean development.

paper_predict_wins_budget_accumulator_qu.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 Predict-Wins source-loop constructor: if every selected winner is
chosen from the ready set computed at its processed prefix, then the
prefix-form budgeted accumulator quota premise follows.
paper_predict_wins_budget_accumulator_qu.source_location: paper-facing theorem endpoint; proof details are discharged by the underlying Lean development.

paper_predict_losses_candidates.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 Predict-Losses filter: candidates whose strict support from all
candidates, plus the budget, stays below the source first-choice threshold.

paper_predict_losses_transfer_initial_lo.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 Predict-Losses transfer loop: count the initial sorted transferable
prefix that can be moved to the top first-choice candidate while remaining
below quota.

paper_sequence_bounds_cover.statement:
-
Algorithm 7 coverage predicate: every feasible source sequence has at most the
predicted upper number of wins and at least the predicted lower number of
initial losses.

paper_bounded_sequence_family.statement: - Sequence family retained by the Algorithm 7 win/loss bounds.

paper_benefits_via_action.statement: - Definition 5.1: an action benefits a candidate or group when active votes strictly increase in some round before the candidate or group exits.

paper_coalition_all_benefit.statement: - Every candidate in a coalition benefits.

paper_losing_prefix_or_losing_only_shape.statement: - The no-Case-(A) ballot shapes allowed by Theorem 5.4.

paper_theorem5_4_allowed_shape.statement: Theorem 5.4: optimal strategies are characterized based on Case (A), with selfish, altruistic-to-loser, and sometimes altruistic-to-winner ballot forms.

paper_theorem5_4_strategy_characterizati.statement: Theorem 5.4: optimal strategies are characterized based on Case (A), with selfish, altruistic-to-loser, and sometimes altruistic-to-winner ballot forms.

paper_always_expost_beneficial.statement: - A strategy benefits the actor in every realized state.

paper_may_be_expost_disadvantageous.statement: - A strategy is disadvantageous in at least one realized state.

paper_eliminated_early_by_margin_less_th.statement:
-
Proposition 5.6 concrete non-selfish downside witness: the strategist is
eliminated before the beneficiary by a margin smaller than the added votes.

paper_round_winning_candidates_never_ele.statement: - Paper Lemma B.2 predicate: round-winning candidates are never election losers.

paper_feasible_sequence_win_count_bound.statement: - Paper Proposition 3.3 win-count boundary: feasible sequences have at most `k` round-winning positions.

paper_feasible_sequence_family_win_bound.statement: - Paper Proposition 3.3 feasibility predicate for a sequence family: every feasible sequence has between one and `k` round-winning positions.
